experiments.title: Attribute a required helper on the selected Dock route
experiments.priority: Nearest useful evidence; reuse owner work, not a new #44 runner
experiments.claim: Whether an exact i386 process is required by the selected game phase, rather than merely installed.
prerequisites: Owner-selected original Dock/client/game/prerequisite identities and invocation phase; current no-account failure cannot prove later absence.
A separately approved next #11 run, existing APISession/supervisor ownership and the actual available #10 coverage contract.
Do not repeat current failures only to restate them; consume new owner evidence when available.
inputs: Selected SteamService.exe SHA-256 72a406a6a2d3e282ab4b468ed8bfadf171fdd03a97969d6214a5da6fdb8dbd03 (i386); its necessity is unknown.
Exact owner-selected Wine services.exe and game CEG/prerequisite manifest are still missing, not inferred from paths.
experiments.interface: Consume #11 sanitized selected-component/launch receipts through its reviewed existing adapters. No new callable or command is selected by #44.
positive: Bind phase, parent/process instance, exact helper bytes/machine and the required action to observed invocation and its outcome.
Record complete required-set coverage if concluding that a phase uses no i386 helper; an earlier failure cannot support that conclusion.
refusal: Missing process/module interval, unselected helper or incomplete prerequisite/CEG evidence -> unknown, never x64-only success.
A required helper that cannot run -> blocker for that phase; no skip, service-disable shortcut or fake readiness.
Helper exit zero without SCM readiness is insufficient.
experiments.resources: Owner-approved finite run/output limits and measured selected closure; no additional #44 native work.
experiments.cleanup: Only the actual owner may reap its child/process group; preserve pre-existing SCM/client processes and unrelated sentinel. Keep failures and cleanup gaps.
experiments.retention: Allowlisted file hashes, phase/parent/required classification, coverage gaps and outcome; no account/session identifiers or raw private traces.
experiments.decision: If required i386 execution is demonstrated, prepare targeted FEX/Wine contracts E1-E4 for review. Otherwise retain unknowns and continue #11 without a broad WoW64 gate.

experiments.title: Isolated low-address ordinary host-NX feasibility
experiments.priority: Smallest conditional host diagnostic; design approval first
experiments.owner: Separately assigned runtime/host owner coordinated with #11
experiments.claim: Whether a bounded low identity-address data reservation can coexist with Pear on the selected host without replacing unowned mappings.
prerequisites: A reviewed original C fixture and allocator/query adapter, exact source/compiler/SDK/executable hashes, per-executable current authorization, reviewed run contract.
One existing high MAP_JIT owner remains unchanged; no second JIT owner or adopted guest-offset ABI.
Select actual usable aligned addresses from availability; do not assume 0x00400000 or any hint is free.
inputs: Original redistributable NX-only host fixture; no Steam or game input.
Selected macOS/architecture/page geometry, actual mapping/protection query results, candidate reservation policy and source identity.
experiments.interface: Design work: a new bounded case using existing owned native supervision/authorization primitives. tools/wine/pe_arena_probe.py contains executable/fault modes and is not this diagnostic or an approved command.
positive: Reserve at most 64 MiB aggregate ordinary host-NX data below 0x80000000 with checked end/size/alignment; query actual RW/NX, write/read owned bytes and release.
Observe unchanged high-owner base/identity/generation/protection before/after when a high owner is present; standalone host success without it has the narrower claim only.
Exercise bounded owned reservation reuse and clean rollback without changing unowned mappings.
refusal: Owned occupied-range control must fail without replacement and preserve its sentinel bytes; never MAP_FIXED over unowned memory.
Invalid alignment, range overflow, unavailable range, budget exhaustion and injected partial setup failure yield explicit error plus cleanup.
Protection query unavailable -> unknown/refused; do not execute data or deliberately fault native code to establish NX.
Busy/stale domain or generation request is rejected; no release of another owner.
experiments.resources: Proposed initial <=64 MiB aggregate low reservation/commit including control ranges, below 2 GiB; one owned child per case, at most 12 declared cases, 10 seconds per child and 256 KiB output per case. Supervisory termination/drain limits must be bound to the reviewed owner contract. This is not measured Steam capacity.
experiments.cleanup: Release only owned ranges after readers/writers retire; query release, preserve unowned sentinel and high owner; retain original failure if cleanup also fails.
experiments.retention: Source/binary/candidate hash, actual queried intervals/protections, OS errors, conflict/refusal and before/after ownership/cleanup receipts.
experiments.decision: Pass establishes only host feasibility. Failure at one tested layout does not prove all low-address designs impossible. Neither outcome authorizes E2 or a memory ABI.

experiments.title: PE32 parser plus actual Wine owner mapping at admitted low bases
experiments.priority: Conditional after concrete owner/PE32 design approval
experiments.owner: One shared Wine loader owner; accepted #40 baseline first
experiments.claim: Whether exact PE32 semantics and canonical Wine bookkeeping work in the proposed candidate, including original fixed-base images.
prerequisites: E1 is a feasibility input, not integrated admission. Review owner/base/role/domain/generation/32-bit fields, publication, rollback, low range and cleanup first.
Construct the accepted #40 ordered source and recheck any later accepted #11 overlapping patch preimages.

Review a PE32 extension to existing parser/fixture machinery; current tests/wine/test_pe_arena.py materializes older publication/cookie patches, so do not call it proof of the final composed candidate.
inputs: New original redistributable PE32 relocatable fixture with source/build/hash receipt, imports, known load-config/cookie layout and four-byte canary-surrounded targets.
Original fixed-base, non-LAA, relocation-stripped fixture; two genuinely available admitted low bases for the relocatable fixture.

Unchanged SteamSetup.exe 2380800 bytes, SHA-256 7d3654531c32d941b8cae81c4137fc542172bfa9635f169cb392f245a0a12bcb, preferred base 0x00400000, only for separately approved original-image parsing/admission; never add synthetic relocations.
Existing original PE32+/ARM64X and #40 required/ceiling/beyond/failed-attach controls.
experiments.interface: Design work: extend existing parser and image-admission tooling against the actual composed candidate; no ready PE32 CLI exists here. Split parser-only results from actual Wine reserve/map/protect/query/free/unmap results.
positive: At two admitted low bases, HIGHLOW changes exactly four bytes to the expected value and preserves adjacent canaries; image/import/load-config addresses remain representable.
Validate PE32 security-cookie pointer width and complete field/directory bounds, initialized value and legal storage protection; retain PE32+ eight-byte controls.
Fixed-base fixture loads only at its available preferred base within non-LAA limits; actual Wine views/server and owner records agree through reserve/commit/protect/query/unmap/release.
Unchanged #40 64 MiB image bound and high owner stay valid; parser pass alone does not claim guest execution.
refusal: Malformed/truncated optional header, directory or load config; incorrect field width; unsupported relocation type; malformed/duplicate/overlapping relocations; target overflow/out-of-image or metadata overlap -> precise refusal.
Relocation arithmetic follows reviewed Windows 32-bit semantics; distinguish legal modulo arithmetic from invalid mapped address/size overflow, with independent expected values.
Occupied preferred address for relocation-stripped/non-LAA fixture -> refuse without relocation or overwrite; preserve the occupying mapping.
Failure after reserve/map/prepare/publication/attach rolls back only owned state and preserves canonical VM error plus cleanup status.
experiments.resources: Proposed parser-only limits: fixture <=8 MiB, 5 seconds and 256 KiB output per case. Actual loader cases: initial low budget <=64 MiB, 20 seconds and 1 MiB output per child, with the reviewed owner cleanup contract. Bound case manifest and measured build/disk budget before execution; do not apply fixture file caps to proprietary installer/desktop capacity.
experiments.cleanup: All successful and refused paths retire source/translation references before range reuse; no stale view, published mapping, handle or owner record remains.
experiments.retention: Exact composed-source/patch preimages, producer/fixture hashes, parser statuses, field/canary bytes and actual Wine/owner before-after events.
experiments.decision: Only complete mapping/cleanup evidence permits proposing i386 guest entry. Original installer execution remains a later separate route test.

experiments.title: Original i386 execution and lifecycle fixtures
experiments.priority: Conditional after admitted source/owner and a reviewed WoW64 adapter
experiments.owner: FEX/Wine runtime owner; coordinate #6 and #42 boundaries
experiments.claim: Whether i386 dispatch, Windows ABI and lifetime semantics work beyond initial CPU entry.
prerequisites: Actual i386 builtin ntdll/import closure, native wow64/wow64win/CPU module and complete host target identities.
Preserve unsupported guards until each concrete implementation/contract is approved; no wholesale removal.

Redistributable original i386 fixtures and independent same-byte native x86 reference where meaningful; reference host availability is not checked. A native x86 CPU Windows WoW64 reference must identify its actual architecture.
inputs: Fixed fixture source/assembler/compiler/oracle bytes and expected event sequences; no proprietary files.
Final Wine/FEX candidate, thread/context/exception/notification producer identities, affected #6 reference receipts.
experiments.interface: Design work: reuse the current CPU capture/comparison and owned Wine/FEX supervision machinery with separately reviewed i386 cases/adapter. Existing x64 command results are not i386 qualification.
positive: Exit/syscall and Unix-call return values, calling convention/stack cleanup, 32-bit register/address/handle semantics.
Two-thread GDT/FS/TLS isolation and join/retirement; repeat thread creation without stale identities.
Handled guest exception and resumption with expected registers/flags and x87/XMM state; original unaligned guest access including the reviewed boundary case.
Guest->host->guest callback and nested/re-entrant return; required cross-thread callback behavior with actual thread identity and buffer lifetime.
Dirty/protect/free/map/unmap invalidation, rewrite/retranslation, unload and same-address reuse under a new generation; no stale compiled link or active callback released early.
refusal: Unsupported context/segment/ISA behavior stays unsupported; AVX/XSTATE is #42, not silently exposed.
Foreign/stale thread or generation, busy retirement, callback after release and invalid notification pairing -> attributable refusal without host fatal fault.
Missing native reference, wrong fixture/candidate hash, incomplete callback/exception event or lost observer interval -> unqualified.
Do not substitute native fatal-fault/no-TEB routes or aligned/static fixture successes for original guest cases.
experiments.resources: Proposed initial per-case bound: 20 seconds and 4 MiB combined output per owned child, two guest workers for thread/TLS/callback cases, finite declared iteration counts. Separate affected existing ordering regression retains its original 32768-pair scope. Review measured candidate/build space before any native work.
experiments.cleanup: Drain callbacks and invalidate links before unload; join/reap owned children/threads, balance handles/leases and preserve unrelated processes and original failures.
experiments.retention: Original fixture hashes, independent reference environment/oracles, per-case comparison and refusals, actual native/guest module identities, lifecycle and cleanup receipts.
experiments.decision: Pass qualifies only the named i386 fixture set on that candidate; it does not qualify Steam desktop or an actual required helper.

experiments.title: Execute only a demonstrated required original i386 helper
experiments.priority: Conditional #11 integration, not broad desktop admission
experiments.owner: #11 with accepted runtime correction and #10 coverage
experiments.claim: Whether the actual required helper completes its function and preserves the genuine game/client session.
prerequisites: E0 identifies required helper/phase and unchanged original bytes; E2/E3 plus all affected regressions qualify the new candidate.
Review actual process/service supervision and per-executable authorization; existing manager may not own a pre-existing SCM/service.
Any real account action requires the owner current approval and existing authentication path, not inherited downloader login.
inputs: Exact selected helper, dependencies, invocation arguments and required readiness/outcome predicate from #11 receipts.
Normal selected Dock/client/game context and candidate hashes; actual service binary selection rather than system32/path inference.
experiments.interface: Extend/reuse the reviewed #11 route adapter under its owner. No duplicated auth client, observer, supervisor or full runner.
positive: Required helper action and readiness succeed with attributable original process/module closure, return and cleanup.
Normal genuine Valve launch leads to the owning-account App ID session and required original-game API/callback outcomes; retain failed/unknown phases separately.
refusal: Exit-zero-only, DLL-load-only, global-user-only, launch-only or menu-only evidence does not establish complete Steamworks.
Unavailable entitlement/session or disconnect yields real failure; never forge success, add supported steam_appid.txt or alter game/Valve bytes.
Any required Rosetta host component or coverage gap blocks Rosetta-free qualification.
experiments.resources: Owner-selected finite helper/run/output bounds and measured dependency/prefix storage, preserved original files and saves.
experiments.cleanup: Only owned process/service instances stopped/reaped; preserve pre-existing client/SCM, original files and account state; record unresolved cleanup.
experiments.retention: Sanitized required-phase outcomes, module/slice/translation coverage and ownership/session assertion results without identifiers, tokens or tickets.
experiments.decision: Success addresses the named helper route only. Other desktop i386 components remain a separate capability.

experiments.title: Reconsider existing native bridge only after a compatible entry review
experiments.priority: Deferred alternative; not the next runtime implementation recommendation
experiments.owner: Separately approved bridge evaluation with #11/#10 contracts
experiments.claim: Whether reusable existing wrappers can support unchanged Windows-game semantics through an entirely Rosetta-free genuine native Steam session.
prerequisites: First present a source-level entry design that does not rewrite Valve/game images or modify installed Steam/CrossOver, and passes Pear source/lifetime contracts. None is selected here.
Pin complete build/SDK/header/Unix-call dependencies and file-specific terms; reconcile NotProton Wine 2df1ee... with Pear, retain upstream languages.
Read-only inventory of explicitly selected non-authenticated native client/helper/library bytes may screen architecture, but cannot substitute dynamic complete required closure.
A later execution scope must authorize its exact fixtures/client/account operations and original game selection separately.
inputs: NotProton c3a49486c14cdf6b9716e2e7ac55286aa537fcf1 and Proton 164e0ccd2ea2b1ec2e5d08dc97f65b184c2539ca wrappers/conversions; full dependency closure remains missing.
Actual original game interface versions, callback IDs/layouts and session requirements, not just the representative Apps008/SteamClient021/LobbyCreated example.
experiments.interface: No runnable bridge command is proposed: existing detour/compat_run/build scripts are outside the approved adoption scope. After a compatible design, separately review source build, layout/callback fixture, then original-game session experiments.
positive: Source-built selected ARM64 host components and Windows wrappers match their pinned ABI/layout tests, including callback payload and asynchronous result lifetime.
Original game reaches real ownership/session methods; callback polling, nested/thread return, shutdown/disconnect/reconnect and call-result failure behave correctly.
Every required actual Steam/helper/bridge/Wine/FEX native process/library is observed on ARM64 without Rosetta for the required interval; no incomplete late-load coverage.
refusal: Valve image rewrite or commercial installed-binary dependency -> outside candidate scope, not a passing experiment.
Wrong/unsupported interface, layout, late callback, shutdown race, failed call result or genuine entitlement/session failure -> real refusal, not success substitute.
Native launcher, ARM64 SDK slice, successful init or downloader authentication alone -> insufficient.
Required Intel-only host component or unobserved required interval -> route not qualified.
experiments.resources: Source-first review before full acquisition/build; enumerate missing artifacts and measured disk/time/output bounds. No cost estimate inferred from macOS Steam availability.
experiments.cleanup: Own only isolated evaluation artifacts/processes; no installed-client patches; preserve originals/account state, release pipes/users/callback buffers and retain failures.
experiments.retention: Complete candidate and client pins, real interface/layout results, sanitized session outcomes, process/module closure, dependency notices and update regression checklist.
experiments.decision: Only new compatible-entry plus measured evidence reopens route comparison. Current source availability does not justify adopting or claiming this route easier.

Original fixed-base installer admission, i386 lifecycle qualification, selected complete mixed-bitness dependencies and reviewed authenticated execution scope.

experiments.interface: No desktop implementation or execution command is selected by #44. Reuse existing owned supervision and Steam authentication interfaces after design review.
positive: Original bootstrap/install/update/startup and genuine sign-in/game launch complete with full required module/child observation.
refusal: Fixed-base conflict, unsupported helper/ABI or required Rosetta process remains a route failure; no binary edits or bypass of services/ownership.
